nodes.label: STORM System
nodes.rationale: Synthesis of Topic Outlines through Retrieval and Multi-perspective Question Asking; automates pre-writing stage for Wikipedia-like article generation.

nodes.label: Perspective-Guided Question Asking
nodes.rationale: Discovers diverse perspectives by surveying related Wikipedia articles, then uses these perspectives to guide LLM question generation for more in-depth research.

nodes.label: Simulated Conversations (Expert-Writer)
nodes.rationale: Multi-turn dialogue where LLM-powered writer asks questions and expert answers grounded on Internet sources; enables iterative research and follow-up questions.

nodes.label: Outline Creation and Refinement
nodes.rationale: Two-stage process: generate draft outline from topic alone, then refine using collected conversations to create comprehensive multi-level section structure.

nodes.label: FreshWiki Dataset
nodes.rationale: Curated dataset of recent high-quality Wikipedia articles (B-class or above) created/edited after LLM training cutoff to avoid data leakage.

nodes.label: Heading Soft Recall Metric
nodes.rationale: Evaluates outline coverage using cosine similarity of Sentence-BERT embeddings between generated and human-written article headings.

nodes.label: Heading Entity Recall Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures percentage of named entities in human-written article headings covered by generated outline, using FLAIR NER.

nodes.label: Outline-driven RAG (oRAG) Baseline
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-augmented generation baseline that searches with topic to generate outline, then searches with section titles for section-by-section article generation.

nodes.label: Human Evaluation with Wikipedia Editors
nodes.rationale: Expert evaluation by 10 experienced Wikipedia editors (500+ edits, 1+ years experience) on 20 article pairs using 1-7 scale rubric.

nodes.label: Red Herring Fallacy Issue
nodes.rationale: Generated articles introduce unverifiable connections between information pieces; goes beyond factual hallucination to improper inferential linking.

nodes.label: Source Bias Transfer Problem
nodes.rationale: Generated articles inherit emotional language and lack neutrality from Internet sources; addresses need for bias mitigation in pre-writing stage.

nodes.label: Citation Quality Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Uses Mistral 7B-Instruct to check entailment; STORM achieves 84.83% citation recall and 85.18% precision; errors stem from improper inference rather than hallucination.

nodes.label: Verifiability Beyond Hallucination
nodes.rationale: Main verifiability issues are improper inferential linking (47%) and inaccurate paraphrasing (14%), not factual hallucination; requires high-level sensemaking.

nodes.label: Ablation: Perspective Component
nodes.rationale: Removing perspective guidance reduces heading soft recall from 86.26% to 84.49% (GPT-3.5); shows perspectives improve but conversation is more critical.

nodes.label: Ablation: Conversation Component
nodes.rationale: Removing multi-turn conversation (asking all questions at once) drops heading soft recall from 86.26% to 77.97%; iterative research is crucial.

nodes.label: Ablation: Outline Stage
nodes.rationale: Removing outline stage (direct article generation) significantly deteriorates all metrics; outline provides essential structure for long-form generation.

nodes.label: Direct Generation Baseline
nodes.rationale: Baseline that directly prompts LLM to generate outline without research; produces basic 'What/When/Where' questions, lacks depth and coverage.

nodes.label: RAG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-augmented generation baseline that searches with topic and uses results to generate outline; unorganized information makes outline generation harder.

nodes.label: Wikipedia Editor Feedback
nodes.rationale: 70% of editors find STORM helpful for pre-writing; 80% think it helps editing new topics; identifies practical utility despite quality gaps vs human articles.
